transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Product), Jordan Lee (VentraCloud Head of Platform), Samir Patel (VentraCloud DevOps), Mei Chen (VentraCloud Solutions Architect), Rita Gomez (VentraCloud Marketplace PM)

Summary:
Short sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture adjustments for VentraCloud images, and joint solution packaging. Action items and a follow-up reference-arch review scheduled. Discussed security gating (KMS/HSM), network models (VPC peering vs private link), and runtime compatibility (ARM vs x86, quantized models).

Topics:
- Marketplace listing checklist and required artifacts
- Reference architecture: private deployment vs marketplace AMI/Container approach
- Joint solution: integration points, billing hooks, and support matrix
- Security/compliance: audit logs, KMS integration, SSO/SAML, RBAC
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Alex Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick intro from our side, I'm Alex, AE on the Partners team, with Priya our SE and Liam from product.
[00:00:15] Jordan Lee: Hi all, Jordan here. Thanks for coordinating. Rita and Samir and Mei are with me. We're excited to get Redwood onto VentraCloud marketplace.
[00:00:28] Priya Sharma: Cool, quick agenda, we'll run through the listing checklist, then dive into the reference arch options, then security and next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:35] Mei Chen: Sounds good. Also we want to clarify if Redwood requires a dedicated private runtime or can run as a marketplace AMI/container with our networking.
[00:00:47] Alex Morales: Great question. There are a few options — hosted Redwood API via our managed offering, Dedicated reserved pools, or a private marketplace image that customers can deploy. For marketplace listing we usually provide both a container image and a reference-arch doc for VPC deployments.
[00:01:05] Samir Patel: For VentraCloud, the marketplace standard is an AMI/VM image or a container image in our registry. Our customers prefer one-click deploy for trial. Do you support an ARM build? A lot of our nodes are Ampere-based.
[00:01:19] Priya Sharma: We do support ARM but, uh, depends on the model/quantization profile. Some models run better x86. We'll need to verify model compatibility and quantization artifacts. I'll add a compatibility matrix we use.
[00:01:32] Jordan Lee: Also curious on license/bring-your-own-model — is the marketplace listing for Redwood managed service or can customers bring their own model via S3 bucket references?
[00:01:44] Liam O'Connor: From a product standpoint, the marketplace listing can be either a managed endpoint integration (we route to Redwood hosted for the customer) or a deployable package. For deployable, we provide a control plane agent and runtime image; customers can point to a model store. We'll detail options in the reference architecture.
[00:01:58] Rita Gomez: For VentraCloud marketplace governance we need a clear support matrix, pricing hooks, and billing integration. Do you expose metering endpoints?
[00:02:09] Alex Morales: Yes, Redwood exposes usage/metering APIs and we can provide a billing webhook for marketplace chargeback. We'll include sample payloads in the listing artifacts.
[00:02:20] Mei Chen: On security, we need SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration, and log/export for audit. Also SSO is required for enterprise tenants — either SAML or OIDC.
[00:02:33] Priya Sharma: We have SOC2 Type II, and support KMS integrations (customer-managed keys). Our private deployments can integrate with HSM/KMS. SSO via SAML and OIDC is supported; for marketplace deployable packages, SAML configuration is handled at tenant setup.
[00:02:49] Samir Patel: Network-wise, question on private connectivity — can Redwood runtime be configured behind a private link or do we need VPC peering? Some customers restrict internet egress.
[00:03:01] Priya Sharma: We support multiple models — private link, VPC peering, and also offline/on-prem package. For the marketplace packaging, the reference arch will show VPC peering and an option for private link. We'll note egress requirements for model downloads.
[00:03:15] Jordan Lee: Perf question — typical latency/throughput numbers for the smallest Dedicated profile vs hosted? Our customers care about 95th percentile.
[00:03:26] Liam O'Connor: Typical numbers: hosted baseline ~80-120ms for small workloads, Dedicated optimized can hit ~40-80ms depending on model and seq length. But, you know, model and tokenization affect numbers. Also quantization helps reduce memory and inference time.
[00:03:44] Priya Sharma: We'll propose recommended inf profiles for common models and a quantization recommendation for each. Note: those numbers assume NVidia x86 hardware; on Ampere ARM numbers might differ 10-30%.
[00:03:58] Mei Chen: Good callout, we need to make sure the listing clarifies hardware assumptions.
[00:04:05] Alex Morales: We'll include a compatibility table. Priya, can you follow up with a short doc that maps models, quant, expected latency on x86 vs Ampere?
[00:04:13] Priya Sharma: Yep, I'll pull our bench numbers and include the caveat for sequence lengths.
[00:04:20] Jordan Lee: On observability — per-route tracing, token-level cost reports — we need sample dashboard screenshots or a CSV export we can show to marketplace ops.
[00:04:31] Liam O'Connor: We can provide screenshots and CSV sample exports. Also, there's an API to pull cost/latency per key.
[00:04:39] Rita Gomez: The marketplace listing needs marketing assets too — short descriptions, logos, and a short how-to. We'll confirm asset sizes.
[00:04:47] Alex Morales: We'll supply a standard set: 1-page overview, 2x screenshots, 1 architecture diagram, and a sample quickstart.
[00:04:56] Samir Patel: About billing hooks, does Redwood support per-token or per-inference billing? We need to map to our metering.
[00:05:06] Alex Morales: We bill per-token for hosted; for private deployments we can export usage and integrate with partner billing. For marketplace, typical approach is meters exposed and VentraCloud charges customers and remits to Redwood per negotiated terms. We'll include webhook spec.
[00:05:20] Mei Chen: A more technical note: our registry uses OCI compliant images and we prefer containers over AMIs for multi-arch. Can you produce an OCI image and manifest for ARM/x86?
[00:05:33] Priya Sharma: Yes, we can produce multi-arch manifests, but some models might not be available in quantized ARM binaries. We'll flag those.
[00:05:43] Jordan Lee: About legal/procurement, we'll need a standard SOW template and SOC2 attestation to attach to listing. Who does that go to?
[00:05:53] Alex Morales: Send those to me, and Liam will route to legal. We'll also share our standard partner SOW and support SLAs.
[00:06:02] Rita Gomez: Are there any sandbox limits for trials? Marketplace customers expect a trial tier.
[00:06:09] Liam O'Connor: We can provide trial keys with quotas; we'll include limits and expiration in the listing.
[00:06:17] Priya Sharma: Quick flag — for private deployments, we need to ensure telemetry and logs don't contain sensitive PII by default. We'll document retention and opt-out controls.
[00:06:28] Mei Chen: Good, that's important for regulated customers.
[00:06:33] Samir Patel: One operational quirk we saw: some customers' NAT gateways block large model downloads. Can we support a staged download or pre-baked images?
[00:06:44] Priya Sharma: We can supply pre-baked images/AMIs or a staged download component. We'll call out the sizing and an option to host model artifacts in VentraCloud's object store to avoid egress.
[00:06:58] Jordan Lee: For the joint reference-arch, could you include a flow for warm cache and KV caching strategy? Some customers need cold-start guarantees.
[00:07:08] Priya Sharma: Absolutely — we'll include KV cache recommendations, warmup scripts, and suggestions for prefetching model prefixes.
[00:07:17] Alex Morales: Ok let's go through a rough checklist so we capture artifacts. I'll read items and Rita please mark who owns what.
[00:07:25] Alex Morales: Listing assets, technical reference-arch doc, multi-arch image, compatibility matrix, security docs (SOC2/KMS), metering webhook spec, support SLAs, trial quota config.
[00:07:37] Rita Gomez: I can own the marketplace-specific items like trial quota config and marketing assets.
[00:07:42] Samir Patel: I'll provision the test account and share secure creds with Alex.
[00:07:46] Mei Chen: I'll validate the network model and confirm whether private link or VPC peering is preferred per customer segments.
[00:07:52] Jordan Lee: I'll coordinate internally for billing mapping and legal touchpoints.
[00:07:57] Alex Morales: Great. Priya will handle compatibility matrix and quant notes, Liam will share SOW and product screenshots.
[00:08:04] Priya Sharma: Yup. I'll also add notes on how latency numbers differ on Ampere.
[00:08:09] Liam O'Connor: We'll prepare a short joint reference-arch (1-2 pages) and a more detailed 6-8 page doc for customers.
[00:08:16] Rita Gomez: Timeline question — how soon can Redwood provide the multi-arch image and listing YAML? We have a marketplace cutover sprint next week.
[00:08:26] Alex Morales: We can get a draft listing YAML and checklist by Monday (2026-06-28). Multi-arch image depends on model artifacts; initial container with control plane agent we can provide in ~1 week (2026-07-02) as long as Samir provisions test environment.
[00:08:40] Mei Chen: Ok that's reasonable.
[00:08:44] Jordan Lee: Any blockers around data residency? Some customers require EU-only hosting.
[00:08:50] Liam O'Connor: We support regional deployments and can provide regional AMIs/images or gated hosted endpoints in specific regions. We'll document options and recommendations.
[00:09:00] Priya Sharma: Also note that for private keys and KMS usage, we can integrate with VentraCloud KMS or customer-managed KMS. We'll include key rotation notes.
[00:09:10] Samir Patel: From an ops perspective we'll want a quickstart that shows health checks, autoscaling config, and recommended machine types.
[00:09:18] Priya Sharma: We'll include health-check endpoints, recommended HPA policies for Kubernetes, and autoscaling knobs for Redwood Dedicated and private deployments.
[00:09:28] Alex Morales: Great. Any final questions?
[00:09:31] Mei Chen: One small one — do you support policy-based routing to fallback to a cheaper model variant if capacity constrained? We want to show customers cost-savings strategies.
[00:09:42] Liam O'Connor: Yes, our routing supports fallback to compatible model variants, region-based routing, and cost-tier fallbacks. We'll include config examples.
[00:09:52] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks team.
[00:09:55] Alex Morales: Ok we'll recap and close.
[00:09:58] Alex Morales: Recap: Alex to share listing checklist and sample YAML (due 6/28), Priya to send compatibility matrix and quant notes (due 7/2), VentraCloud (Samir) to provision test account (due 7/5), Rita to consolidate marketplace asset requirements (due 6/30), schedule reference-arch review w/ security (target 7/8).
[00:10:22] Jordan Lee: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[00:10:26] Alex Morales: Thanks all.
[00:10:29] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (eg "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), speaker overlaps, and filler words were left intact to preserve realism.
